text: You're pushing your cart down a cramped grocery aisle, dodging others. You just want to grab your items and leave; it's a frustrating battle for space.
Then you step into a different store. Suddenly, the aisles are wide, open, almost empty. So much room, you could practically do a cartwheel.
You might think, 'Great for carts!' or 'Just more space!' But that’s a naive view. The real system at play is far more subtle.
The real reason: wide aisles are a subtle trick. They encourage you to slow down, relax, browse comfortably, increasing your time in the store.
This extra time, this relaxed browsing, isn't just for you. It means you’re more likely to see and buy impulse items, adding more to your cart.
So next time you navigate those spacious aisles, remember: you’re not just shopping. You're part of a system engineered to make you spend a little more.
